 CHARLOTTE, N.C. , Jan. 14, 2021 /PRNewswire/  Nucor Corporation (NYSE: NUE) announced today that Executive Vice President of Raw Materials, Craig A. Feldman , plans to retire in June of this year after 35 years of service with Nucor and The David J. Joseph Company (DJJ).  

  Mr. Feldman began his career as a Brokerage Representative for DJJ in 1986, subsequently serving as District Manager of DJJs Salt Lake City brokerage office, Commercial Vice President at DJJs subsidiary, Western Metals Recycling LLC (WMR), and President of WMR.  Mr. Feldman served on the operational staff of DJJs then-owner in the Netherlands from 2005 until his 2007 appointment as DJJs Executive Vice President, Recycling Operations.  Mr. Feldman was promoted to President of DJJ in 2013 and became a Vice President and General Manager of Nucor when DJJ was acquired by Nucor in 2008.  He was promoted to Executive Vice President of Nucor in 2018 and continued to serve as President of DJJ until the end of last year.  Nucor previously announced the appointment of Mark D. Schaefer , another 35-year veteran of DJJ, as President of DJJ, effective January 1, 2021 .

  Effective February 1, 2021 , Daniel R. Needham will be promoted to Executive Vice President of Bar and Rebar Fabrication Products.  Mr. Needham began his career with Nucor in 2000 as Controller at Nucor Steel Hertford County.  He subsequently served as Controller of Nucor Steel Decatur, LLC and Nucor Steel Utah.  In 2011, Mr. Needham became General Manager of Nucor Steel Connecticut, Inc.  He later served as General Manager of Nucor Steel Utah and was elected Vice President in 2016.  In 2019, Mr. Needham was promoted to Vice President and General Manager of Nucor Steel Indiana.

His experience across multiple operations and communities strengthened our position in the North American steel industry and helped position the company for continued success. We are grateful for Dan’s many contributions and wish him and his family all the best in the next chapter,” said Leon Topalian, Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Nucor.

## Nucor Financial Overview 2021–2025

Updated Nov 4, 2026

Nucor's earnings per share fell **74%** in four years, from **$28.79** in **FY2022** to $7.52a in **FY2025**, even as net sales slipped only **22%** over the same stretch. That gap is the story: this is a high-operating-leverage steel business where small price swings hit profit hard, and the data now show that cycle turning upward.

The long arc is stark. Net earnings attributable to stockholders climbed to $6.83 billionb in **FY2021** on **$36.48 billion** of sales, a **30%** gross margin, and a **55.0%** return on equity. By **FY2025**, earnings were **$1.74 billion** on **$32.49 billion** of sales. Gross margin collapsed to **13%** in **FY2024**, and the steel products segment, hit by weaker joist and deck pricing, fell to **$1.23 billion** of pretax earnings in **FY2025** from **$4.09 billion** in **FY2022**. Cash from operations dropped from **$10.07 billion** in **FY2022** to **$3.23 billion** in **FY2025**, while capital expenditures rose to **$3.42 billion**, funding the West Virginia sheet mill, now estimated near **$4 billion**.

The balance sheet absorbed the strain. Funded debt to total capital stayed at **24.4%**, and the $2.25 billionc revolver was undrawn. Cash and short-term investments fell to **$2.70 billion** from **$7.13 billion** in **FY2023**. Steel mills backlogs reached **$3.35 billion** at year-end **FY2025**, up from **$2.13 billion**. The market priced in a trough: at the close of **FY2025**, shares traded at **$163.11**, or **21.7x** earnings, a premium multiple on depressed profits.

His experience across multiple operations and communities strengthened our position in the North American steel industry and helped position the company for continued success. We are grateful for Dan’s many contributions and wish him and his family all the best in the next chapter,” said Leon Topalian, Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Nucor.
